name: Overlapping Registration Entries
description: Create multiple registration entries with identical selectors but different SPIFFE IDs, causing a single workload to receive multiple identities and enabling unauthorized service access
real_world_relevance: Eviatar Gerzi (CyberArk) demonstrated that SPIRE's selector-based attestation allows entry ambiguity — if two entries share selectors, a workload silently receives SVIDs for both identities, violating least-privilege

attack_flow.description: Attacker with SPIRE Server registration access creates a second entry using the same selectors as an existing workload, causing the workload to receive an additional SVID it was never intended to hold
diagram: 1. Enumerate existing registration entries to identify target workload
2. Analyze the target entry's selectors (e.g., unix:uid:1000 + unix:path:/usr/bin/app)
3. Create a new entry with the SAME selectors but a different, privileged SPIFFE ID
4. Wait for or trigger workload re-attestation on the SPIRE Agent
5. Workload now receives SVIDs for both its original and the attacker-chosen identity
6. Verify dual identity by fetching X.509 SVIDs from the Workload API

immediate: Rotate SVIDs for all affected workloads
Audit all registration entries for duplicate selector sets
long_term: Enforce composite selectors (uid + path + sha256) to reduce overlap surface
Implement OPA/Rego admission policies that reject entries sharing selectors with existing entries
Restrict SPIRE Server registration API to CI/CD pipelines with audit trails
Deploy the SPIRE identity monitor as a continuous sidecar on all nodes
